app.name: Working hours calculator
app.description: Calculates working time from start, end and break in hours and minutes and as a decimal, with the legal minimum break under German law, weekly total, overtime and gross payout.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate my working time?

acceptedAnswer.text: End minus start minus break. From 7:30 to 16:15 with a 45-minute break you are present for 8 hours 45 minutes, minus 45 minutes, which makes 8:00 hours.

mainEntity.name: How much break am I entitled to by law?

acceptedAnswer.text: For more than 6 and up to 9 hours of work at least 30 minutes, for more than 9 hours at least 45 minutes (Section 4 ArbZG). Young people under 18 need 30 minutes after more than 4.5 hours and 60 minutes after more than 6 hours (Section 11 JArbSchG).

mainEntity.name: Does the break count as working time?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Working time is the time from the start to the end of work without rest breaks (Section 2 (1) ArbZG). The break is only paid if your contract or collective agreement says so.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert hours and minutes into a decimal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the minutes by 60 and add them to the hours: 7 hours 45 minutes are 7 + 45/60 = 7.75 hours.
Only in your browser, so your times are still there on your next visit. Nothing is sent to a server.

azrLede.beginn_ende_und_pause_eintragen: Enter start, end and break, and your working time is there: in hours and minutes and as a decimal. With the legal minimum break, for one day or the whole week, and as a flexitime calculator with overtime and payout if you like.

azrWeiterP.die_zeiterfassung_von_myworkl: MyWorkLog’s time tracking does the same maths automatically: punch clock or manual entry, legal breaks, overtime balance and vacation across the whole year. Free, no account, your data stays on your device.
azrPauseP1.die_rechnung_ist_immer_diesel: The calculation is always the same: end minus start minus break. If you are at work from 7:30 to 16:15, you are present for 8 hours 45 minutes; with a 45-minute break that leaves 8:00 hours of working time. The break does not count as working time (Section 2 (1) ArbZG).
azrPauseP2.laesst_du_das_pausenfeld_leer: If you leave the break field empty, the calculator uses the legal minimum break: 30 minutes for more than 6 hours, 45 minutes for more than 9 hours (Section 4 ArbZG). The break may be split into periods of at least 15 minutes. If you enter less than required, the calculator points it out.
azrPauseP3.fuer_jugendliche_unter_18_gel: Longer breaks apply to young people under 18: 30 minutes for more than 4.5 hours, 60 minutes for more than 6 hours (Section 11 JArbSchG). That is what the “under 18” box above is for.
azrDezP.viele_stundenzettel_und_lohnabre: Many timesheets and payslips use decimal hours, often called “industrial minutes”. Divide the minutes by 60: 7 hours 45 minutes are 7.75 hours. The calculator shows both side by side.
azrWocheP1.mit_tag_hinzufuegen_traegst_d: With “Add day” you can enter up to seven days, and the calculator adds them up to your weekly working time. Enter your target hours for these days, such as 40 for a full-time week, and you immediately see your overtime or shortfall. You can also check a flexitime account this way.
azrWocheP2.erlaubt_sind_werktaeglich_8_s: German law allows 8 hours per working day, up to 10 hours only if this averages out to 8 hours within six months (Section 3 ArbZG). There must be at least 11 hours of rest between two working days (Section 5 ArbZG). The calculator recognises a shift across midnight when the end is before the start.
azrGeldT.ueberstunden_auszahlen_was_der_: Overtime payout: what the calculator shows
azrGeldP1.traegst_du_stundenlohn_und_fal: If you enter your hourly wage and, if agreed, a premium, the calculator works out the amount for your overtime: overtime times hourly wage, plus premium. There is no statutory overtime premium in Germany; it is set in the collective or employment contract.
azrGeldP2.der_betrag_ist_brutto_was: The amount is gross. What is left net depends on tax class, church tax and social security contributions, and an honest calculator cannot know that without those details.
azrGeldP3.fuer_azubis_gilt_jede_stunde: For trainees: every hour beyond the agreed training time must be paid separately or compensated with time off (Section 17 (7) BBiG).
